name: What's the difference between paint-grade and stain-grade trim?

mainEntity.name: What's the difference between paint-grade and stain-grade trim?

acceptedAnswer.text: Paint-grade trim is typically made from less expensive woods or MDF and is intended to be painted. It may have minor imperfections or a less prominent grain, as these will be covered by paint. Stain-grade trim, on the other hand, uses higher-quality woods like oak, maple, or cherry, chosen for their attractive grain patterns. It is designed to be stained or clear-coated, allowing the natural beauty of the wood to show through. The choice depends on your desired aesthetic and budget.
acceptedAnswer.description: Paint-grade trim is designed to be painted, often from less expensive materials, while stain-grade uses higher-quality wood to showcase its natural grain with stains or clear coats.
